before: Left, a preview site built by hand in 2020. Right, the card the factory made from its archive: tokens from the Playbook, seven checks on every build, drift named after every deploy, the story on the board. Nothing hand-built.
after: In 2020, Preview Sites were created by hand. Today, a factory generates: an interactive design system, its tokens, and routes from the Playbook. It writes tests and provides knobs to turn and proves its checks on every build. Drift is named, and ADO stories are updated on the board. Nothing is hand-built so we don't wait days or weeks for decisions that can be made in near real-time

before: Since Flash, I have been fighting the good fight that designers should code. Not because engineers cannot design, and not because designers should ship production systems alone, but because a decision made in the medium it will ship in is the only one a room can argue with.
after: Since Flash, I've been fighting the good fight that designers should code. Not because engineers can't design, and not because designers need to ship production code alone, but because a decision made in the medium it ships in reveals more than a static Figma can.

before: Coding is not dead. Manually creating code is. The judgment about what to build, for whom, and what must never regress is the part that got more valuable, and it is the part I have spent nineteen years learning to write down where the next person will find it.
after: Coding is not dead. Manually creating code might be. The judgment about what to build, for whom, and what must never regress is the part that got more valuable. That's the part I have spent two decades years learning to leave where the next person will find it.
